findings.reason: Verified that the old fail-fast on multiple providers is gone, that Default, FIPS1402 and Elytron all return order 200, and that a tie is settled by the stable sort, i.e. ServiceLoader classpath order, with the losers logged only at debug level, so a classpath with both FIPS and default providers would silently pick one; this is a real behaviour regression, though it needs a misconfigured classpath to trigger.

Correct: one default-size EC key is reused for ES256, ES384 and ES512, and the test only round-trips the codec through itself without checking Signature.verify, so a truncation or encoding bug could go undetected; it is still only a test gap with no confirmed defect.
Verified that the two ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls before the real encoding build objects that are never used; this is trivial cleanup.

Correct that adding an abstract order() to the public CryptoProvider interface breaks out-of-tree implementations (they fail to compile, or hit AbstractMethodError during the sort), and a default method would avoid that, but such third-party providers are rare and the finding is phrased as a question.
